**Setup.** Write $f(x)=\prod_{i=1}^{6}(x-r_i)$ with every root $r_i\in(0,1)$, which the hypothesis that all roots are real and lie in $(0,1)$ requires. Since the degree is 6 (even), the constant term is

$$a_0=f(0)=\prod_{i=1}^6(-r_i)=\prod_{i=1}^6 r_i=:P.$$

Because each $r_i\in(0,1)$, we have $P>0$, so $1/P$ is well defined and positive.

**Using the constraint.** The hypothesis $f(0)=f(1)$ gives

$$\prod_{i=1}^6(1-r_i)=f(1)=f(0)=\prod_{i=1}^6 r_i=P.$$

**Bounding $P$.** Multiply the two expressions for $P$:

$$P^2=\prod_{i=1}^6 r_i(1-r_i).$$

For each $i$, AM–GM gives $r_i(1-r_i)\le\left(\frac{r_i+(1-r_i)}{2}\right)^2=\frac14$, with equality iff $r_i=\tfrac12$. Since all factors are positive,

$$P^2\le\left(\tfrac14\right)^6=\tfrac{1}{4096}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad P\le\tfrac{1}{64}.$$

Hence $\dfrac{1}{P}\ge 64$.

**Attainment.** Take $f(x)=\left(x-\tfrac12\right)^6$. Its roots are all real, equal to $\tfrac12\in(0,1)$, and $f(0)=f(1)=\tfrac1{64}$. Its product of roots is $\left(\tfrac12\right)^6=\tfrac1{64}$, so $1/P=64$. The bound is achieved.

**Check of quantifiers.** The bound holds for every admissible $f$ (all roots in $(0,1)$ and $f(0)=f(1)$), and it is attained by an admissible $f$, so the minimum is exactly 64.

Final answer: 64
